params.prompt: Start exactly from the start image (tooth extraction). The forceps holding the tooth move slowly away from the treatment area and leave the frame. The camera glides gently toward the extraction site and continuously settles into the implant procedure of the end image. It must look like a plausible, continuous clinical procedure, not a magical transformation; introduce only objects supported by the end image, entering naturally. End at the exact composition of the end image. RULES: The start and end images are strict visual targets; do not redesign or reinterpret them, animate the existing scenes preserving identity, anatomy, clothing, instruments, devices and environment. 16:9 widescreen, photorealistic premium clinical cinematography. SLOW, gradual, continuous camera movement; let each action finish before the next begins; no fast zooms, rapid rotations, cuts, fades, black frames, flicker or warping. Nobody and nothing appears out of nowhere: every hand, doctor, instrument or device enters and leaves the frame through a visible, physically plausible movement from outside the crop; no objects popping in, teleporting or morphing; no extra people or unrequested props; no text or logos. Anatomically correct hands, fingers, teeth and faces. Consistent lighting, realistic skin and dental textures. Do not reveal areas outside the original crop unless the end image requires it. Start exactly on the first frame and end exactly on the end image composition; prioritize frame-to-frame continuity and reference accuracy over dramatic movement.
